correctness.rationale: The exact forbidden-word cutoffs produce cofinite renewal equations with unambiguous zero-run indexing. Taylor expansion at the unique positive renewal root gives the uniform normalized entropy tail with controlled derivative error. Telescoped mechanical-word discrepancy, summation by parts, and irrational-rotation density establish strictly increasing discounted phase values and one jump of size (1-r)r^(n-1) at each distinct theta_n; endpoint span and geometric-series normalization prove these are all complementary gaps. Sturmian m+1 factor complexity gives Hausdorff dimension zero, and dense jumps plus endpoint approach yield perfectness. SFT strict-entropy principle proves plateau strictness. The reproducible check.py passed 18,414 direct local-window language tests, 23 cutoff witnesses, 18 jump evaluations, total jump length, and eight root comparisons; finite checks are not used as proof of all slopes.

value.rationale: The natural canonical-cover entropy error probes how finite forbidden-word information approximates dynamical complexity. The exact all-irrational-slope complementary gap census for its normalized phase set reveals a substantial structural phenomenon, not a routine finite table or arbitrary parameter slice: one geometric gap per rotation breakpoint, a zero-dimensional perfect limit set, exact hull scale, and strict plateau positions. These sharp geometric invariants are not implied by a general entropy-root approximation and distinguish Sturmian-indexed gaps from periodic or geometric-indexed cases.
